costPage.introEmpty: 10X Health System publishes no price list. Testing, IV drips, peptides and supplements are billed separately, and a wellness concierge quotes the protocol once a provider has read your results. PRP and extracellular vesicle treatments at the affiliated HealthGAINS clinic are quoted the same way, so the number you get depends on what the panel finds rather than on a menu.

items.label: Diagnostic testing and gene panel
items.note: Billed on its own before any protocol is designed. Ask which panels are in the quote, since this is where the first invoice usually lands.

items.label: IV drips and nutrient therapy
items.note: Priced per drip. Members and package buyers pay a different rate to walk-ins, so ask for both.

items.label: Peptides and supplements
items.note: Ongoing monthly cost on top of the protocol fee, and the part people underestimate.

items.label: PRP and extracellular vesicle treatment (HealthGAINS)
items.note: Quoted by the affiliated clinic, not by 10X Health directly.

includes: Provider review of your test results
A written protocol built from those results
Concierge follow-up while you are on the protocol
costPage.insuranceNote: This is a cash-pay wellness programme, so insurance does not apply to the testing, the protocol or the drips. Ask whether an itemised receipt is available if you intend to try an HSA or FSA claim.
costPage.financingNote: No published financing programme. Packages and memberships are the usual way the cost is spread, so ask what the difference is between paying per visit and paying up front.

faqs.question: How much does 10X Health System cost?
faqs.answer: There is no published figure. Testing, drips, peptides and supplements are each billed separately, and the total depends entirely on what the provider recommends after reading your panel. Ask for the quote itemised by line rather than as one number.

faqs.question: Is the first consultation free?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book. The pattern here is that the diagnostic panel is the paid first step, and the consultation is the conversation about its results, so the first real cost is usually the testing.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover any of it?
faqs.answer: No. Nothing in this programme is billed to insurance. Some patients recover part of the lab cost through an HSA or FSA, so ask for an itemised receipt.

costPage.introEmpty: AgeRejuvenation does not run a set price list. Regenerative and exosome protocols are quoted per plan after an assessment, and the first consultation is free, so you can get a number before you commit to anything. Hormone, weight loss and IV programmes are billed separately from the cell work.

items.label: Initial consultation and assessment
items.note: Free. This is where the quote for everything else comes from.

items.label: Exosome therapy
items.note: Quoted per plan. Cost moves with the number of sites treated and how many sessions are scheduled.

items.label: Mesenchymal cell and umbilical cord protocols
items.note: Quoted after the assessment. Ask how many vials the quote covers, since that is the variable that moves the price most.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
items.note: The lower-cost option here, and usually the one recommended first for joints.

items.label: Hormone, weight loss and IV programmes
items.note: Priced and billed apart from the regenerative work.

excludes: Repeat sessions beyond the quoted plan
costPage.insuranceNote: Regenerative treatment is not covered by insurance and is paid out of pocket. Parts of the diagnostic work may be claimable on your own plan, so ask the front desk what they can code before you assume otherwise.
costPage.financingNote: Ask about payment plans at the consultation. Nothing is published, and the answer tends to depend on the size of the protocol.

faqs.question: How much does AgeRejuvenation cost?
faqs.answer: There is no published price. Regenerative and exosome protocols are quoted per plan after an assessment, and the consultation that produces the quote is free.

faqs.question: Is the consultation really free?
faqs.answer: Yes, the first consultation is offered at no cost. That is the visit where you get a figure, so it is a low-risk way to find out what your case would run.

faqs.question: Are hormone and weight loss programmes included?
faqs.answer: No. Those are separate programmes on their own monthly pricing and are billed apart from any regenerative treatment.

costPage.intro: AgelessRx is one of the few names in this category that puts its prices on the page. Everything is a monthly or quarterly subscription with shipping included, from $25 a month at the entry end to $159 a month for microdosed tirzepatide. Video consultations with the prescriber are free, insurance is not accepted, and lab panels and full-dose GLP-1 programmes are priced on their own.

items.label: Metformin
items.note: Billed $75 quarterly. The cheapest way in, and the one most people start on.

items.label: Rapamycin
items.note: Prescribed on assessment. Dosing schedules vary, so confirm what the monthly figure covers.

items.label: NAD+ injection
items.note: $79 a month on a prepaid three month plan, $149 a month after that. The introductory rate is the one advertised.

items.label: Powers Hair Solution
items.note: $95 for the first month, $120 a month after.

items.label: Microdosed tirzepatide
items.note: Microdosing programme. Full-dose GLP-1 programmes are priced separately and cost more.

items.label: Lab panels
items.note: Priced individually and not bundled into any subscription.

items.label: Prescriber video consultation
items.note: Free, and required before a prescription is issued.

includes: Free video consultations with the prescriber
costPage.insuranceNote: Insurance is not accepted. Every subscription is cash pay, which is part of why the published prices are as low as they are.
costPage.financingNote: No financing as such. The quarterly and prepaid plans are the discount mechanism here, so paying further ahead is what lowers the monthly figure.

faqs.question: How much does AgelessRx cost per month?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the medication. Metformin is $25 a month at the low end, NAD+ injections run $79 to $149, and microdosed tirzepatide is $159. Shipping is included in the subscription price.

faqs.question: Do I pay for a consultation?
faqs.answer: No. Video consultations with the prescriber are free. You pay for medication and for any lab panel you order.

faqs.question: Why is NAD+ two different prices?
faqs.answer: $79 a month is the prepaid three month rate. After that block the price goes to $149 a month, so budget on the higher figure if you plan to stay on it.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: No. AgelessRx does not accept insurance for any of its programmes.

costPage.introEmpty: BioReset Medical publishes no prices. The practice states that regenerative medicine treatments are not covered by insurance and that procedures are billed directly to you at the time of service, so the figure comes out of the consultation rather than off a page.

items.label: Regenerative orthopaedic procedures
items.note: Quoted after examination and imaging review. Cost tracks the joint, the number of sites and the cell source used.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
items.note: Typically the lowest-cost option in the range offered here.

items.label: Bone marrow and adipose derived procedures
items.note: Harvest, processing and delivery all sit inside one procedure fee. Ask for that fee itemised.

items.label: Exosome and IV protocols
items.note: Priced per protocol rather than per visit.

includes: Same-day processing and delivery of your own cells where that is the plan
excludes: Any medication or supplement prescribed alongside
costPage.insuranceNote: Regenerative treatments are not covered by insurance and are billed directly to you at the time of service. Ask for a superbill if you intend to try an out-of-network claim.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask at the consultation whether the practice works with a third-party financing partner, since most clinics in this bracket do.

faqs.question: How much does BioReset Medical cost?
faqs.answer: No prices are published. Regenerative procedures are quoted after a consultation and billed directly to you at the time of service.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover regenerative treatment here?
faqs.answer: No. The practice is explicit that these treatments are not covered and that you pay at the time of service.

faqs.question: What moves the price up or down?
faqs.answer: The joint being treated, how many sites are injected in one visit, and which cell source is used. PRP sits at the lower end and bone marrow work at the higher end.

costPage.introEmpty: Biote publishes no patient prices, and the reason is structural: it does not bill patients at all. Each certified clinic sets its own fee for an insertion and its own retail price on Biote supplements, so the number you pay comes from the individual practice, not from Biote. Expect compounded pellets to sit outside insurance coverage wherever you go.

items.label: Pellet insertion
items.note: Set by the certified clinic you attend, not by Biote. Prices vary widely between practices in the same city, so it is worth calling two.

items.label: Biote supplements
items.note: Retail price set by the clinic. Ask whether they are optional or built into the programme.

items.label: Lab work and follow-up
items.note: Billed by the clinic. Ask how many panels a year the protocol expects.

includes: Whatever the individual certified clinic bundles into its insertion fee
excludes: Anything the clinic chooses to bill separately, which commonly means labs and supplements
costPage.insuranceNote: Compounded hormone pellets generally sit outside insurance coverage. Some clinics can bill the office visit or the lab work to insurance even when the pellet itself is cash pay, so ask that question specifically.
costPage.financingNote: Any financing is the individual clinic's, not Biote's. Ask the practice, not the brand.

faqs.question: How much do Biote pellets cost?
faqs.answer: Biote does not set or publish a patient price. Each certified clinic sets its own insertion fee, so the only reliable figure comes from calling the practice you plan to attend.

faqs.question: Why can Biote not tell me the price?
faqs.answer: Because it does not bill patients. Biote certifies and supplies clinics; the clinic is the one that charges you.

faqs.question: Will insurance pay for it?
faqs.answer: Usually not for the pellets themselves. Ask your clinic whether the consultation and lab work can be billed even when the pellet cannot.

costPage.introEmpty: Blatman Health and Wellness Center publishes no prices, but it will send you one. The clinic says cost depends on how many injections are needed and what is being treated, and the office provides a pricing sheet on request, which is more than most practices in this category offer before a visit.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections
items.note: Priced by the number of injection sites rather than as a flat session fee.

items.label: Cell and exosome therapy
items.note: Quoted from the pricing sheet once the clinic knows what is being treated.

items.label: IV protocols
items.note: Billed separately from any injection work.

items.label: Office pricing sheet
items.note: Free. Ask the office to send it before you book, and you will have real figures going into the consultation.

includes: The injections in the quoted plan
The consultation that produces the plan
costPage.insuranceNote: The clinic does not bill insurance, though a superbill is available so you can submit an out-of-network claim yourself. Whether anything comes back depends entirely on your plan.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask when you request the pricing sheet.

faqs.question: How much does Blatman Health and Wellness Center charge?
faqs.answer: No prices are published, but the office will send a pricing sheet on request. Cost depends on how many injections are needed and what is being treated.

faqs.question: Can I get the prices before I book a visit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ask the office to email the pricing sheet. That is unusual in this category and worth using.

faqs.question: Does the clinic bill insurance?
faqs.answer: No, but it provides a superbill so you can file an out-of-network claim yourself.

sources.label: Blatman Health and Wellness Center website

costPage.introEmpty: Boulder Biologics quotes at the consultation rather than from a list. Price depends on the joint, the number of sites and the formulation used. Everything is self-pay because most plans class autologous biologic procedures as investigational, but the clinic works with HSA and FSA funds and offers 0% APR payment plans, which is the practical difference between a $6,000 invoice and a monthly figure.

items.label: Bone marrow concentrate procedure
items.note: Harvest, processing and image-guided injection. The number of joints treated in one visit is the main variable.

items.label: Adipose derived procedure
items.note: Quoted after examination. Ask how the fee changes if a second site is added on the day.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
items.note: The lower-cost tier, and often the recommended starting point.

items.label: Consultation and imaging review
items.note: Where the quote comes from. Ask for it in writing before you leave.

includes: Itemised documentation you can submit to an HSA or FSA administrator
costPage.insuranceNote: Most plans class autologous biologic procedures as investigational and do not cover them, so treat this as self-pay. HSA and FSA funds usually work, and the clinic provides itemised documentation for exactly that purpose.
costPage.financingNote: Payment plans at 0% APR are available. Ask what term is offered and whether the rate holds for the whole term.

faqs.question: How much does Boulder Biologics cost?
faqs.answer: There is no published price. Cost depends on the joint, the number of sites and the formulation, and is quoted at the consultation.

faqs.question: Can I use HSA or FSA money?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. The clinic provides itemised documentation specifically so you can submit it, though your administrator makes the final call.

faqs.question: Is there a payment plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Payment plans at 0% APR are offered. Confirm the term and whether the rate applies for its full length.

faqs.question: Will insurance pay for any of it?
faqs.answer: Most plans will not. Autologous biologic procedures are generally classed as investigational, which is the wording that leads to a denial.

costPage.introEmpty: CELLAXYS has no set price list. Cost is quoted after a consultation and a look at your imaging, because it depends on the joint being treated and which cell source is used. The gap between a PRP session and a bone marrow procedure here is large enough that a number quoted before anyone has seen your scans would be meaningless.

items.label: Bone marrow derived procedure
items.note: Harvest, same-day processing and image-guided injection. Priced by joint.

items.label: Adipose derived procedure
items.note: Quoted after imaging review. Ask whether a second joint on the same day is discounted.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
items.note: The entry tier. Often used as a first step before a cell procedure is considered.

items.label: Consultation and imaging review
items.note: The visit that produces your quote.

includes: Same-day harvest and processing where that is the plan
costPage.insuranceNote: Regenerative procedures of this kind are not covered by US insurance and are paid out of pocket. Ask whether the office visit itself can be billed, which is sometimes possible even when the procedure cannot.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask at the consultation which financing partners the clinic works with.

faqs.question: How much does CELLAXYS cost?
faqs.answer: There is no set price list. Cost is quoted after a consultation and a review of your imaging, since it depends on the joint and the cell source used.

faqs.question: Why does the cell source change the price?
faqs.answer: Bone marrow and adipose procedures involve a harvest and same-day processing, which PRP does not. That work is the difference in the invoice.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: No. Expect to pay out of pocket for the procedure itself.

costPage.introEmpty: California Wellness Institute publishes no prices for any service, exosome therapy and PRP included. The practice quotes after a consultation with Dr. Rajaratnam, and it links to CareCredit from its service pages, which is the clearest signal you have that treatments here are financed rather than paid on the day.

items.label: Exosome therapy
items.note: Quoted after consultation. Cost moves with the area treated and the number of sessions planned.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
items.note: Used for joints, hair and aesthetics here, and the price differs by application. Ask which one your quote covers.

items.label: Consultation with Dr. Rajaratnam
items.note: The visit that produces the quote. Confirm whether it carries a fee when you book.

includes: The treatment as quoted at the consultation
excludes: Anything added after the original plan
costPage.insuranceNote: Aesthetic and regenerative work of this kind is not covered by insurance. Treat the whole quote as out of pocket unless the office tells you otherwise in writing.
costPage.financingNote: CareCredit is linked from the practice's own service pages, so third-party financing is the expected route. Check the promotional term and what rate applies once it ends.

faqs.question: How much does California Wellness Institute cost?
faqs.answer: No prices are published for any service. You get a figure after a consultation with Dr. Rajaratnam.

faqs.question: Can I finance the treatment?
faqs.answer: The practice links to CareCredit from its service pages, so financing is the expected route. Read the promotional period terms carefully.

faqs.question: Does the price change by body area?
faqs.answer: Yes. PRP for hair, skin and joints are different treatments with different quantities involved, and they are quoted separately.

costPage.intro: Cenegenics publishes its own pricing, which is unusual in this category and worth crediting. The Performance Health Assessment runs $4,495 to $13,000 depending on how much testing the physician orders, the programme fee is then $550 to $750 a month, and nutraceuticals and medications add $350 to $600 a month. Cenegenics totals that at an average of $14,000 to $21,000 a year. Insurance is not accepted, though FSA and HSA funds can be used.

items.label: Performance Health Assessment
items.note: The range is entirely down to how much testing your physician orders. Ask which tier you are being quoted and what it adds.

items.label: Programme fee
items.note: Covers physician access, coaching, phlebotomy and lab work.

items.label: Nutraceuticals and medications
items.note: Prescribed as clinically indicated, and billed on top of the programme fee.

items.label: Total annual cost
items.note: Cenegenics' own stated average once the assessment, programme fee and medications are added together.

items.label: Regenerative treatments
items.note: Set by each individual centre rather than nationally, so the figure comes from your local location.

excludes: Regenerative treatments, which each centre prices itself
Anything ordered beyond the assessment tier you bought
costPage.insuranceNote: Cenegenics does not accept insurance. FSA and HSA funds can be used for treatments and medications, which for a programme in this bracket is worth planning a year ahead for.
costPage.financingNote: No published financing programme. The monthly structure is itself the spread, since only the assessment is a large single payment.

faqs.question: How much does Cenegenics cost per year?
faqs.answer: Cenegenics puts the average at $14,000 to $21,000 a year. That is the Performance Health Assessment of $4,495 to $13,000, plus $550 to $750 a month in programme fees, plus $350 to $600 a month in nutraceuticals and medications.

faqs.question: Why is the assessment price such a wide range?
faqs.answer: Because the amount of testing is set by your physician. The low end is the standard panel; the high end reflects a much fuller workup.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover Cenegenics?
faqs.answer: No. Insurance is not accepted, though FSA and HSA funds can be used for treatments and medications.

faqs.question: Are regenerative treatments part of the programme fee?
faqs.answer: No. Those are priced by each individual centre and billed separately from the programme.

costPage.intro: Centeno-Schultz quotes after evaluation rather than from a menu, but the spread is known: roughly $2,000 at the PRP end to about $12,000 for the more involved bone marrow concentrate work. The gap is the procedure, not the clinic. PRP is a draw and an injection; a bone marrow concentrate procedure adds a harvest, processing and precise image-guided placement, sometimes across several structures in one visit.

items.label: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) procedure
items.note: The lower end of the range. Priced by the structure treated and the number of sites.

items.label: Bone marrow concentrate procedure
items.note: The upper end. Includes the marrow harvest, same-day processing and image-guided placement.

items.label: Full range across procedures
items.note: Where quoted cases generally land. Complex multi-level spine work sits at the top of it.

items.label: Evaluation and imaging review
items.note: Candidacy and the quote both come out of this visit.

includes: Same-day harvest and processing on cell procedures
The procedure as quoted after evaluation
costPage.insuranceNote: Interventional orthobiologic procedures are not covered by US insurance and are paid out of pocket. Ask whether the evaluation visit itself can be billed to your plan, which is sometimes possible.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask at the evaluation which financing partners the clinic works with, particularly for the multi-level cases at the top of the range.

faqs.question: How much does Centeno-Schultz cost?
faqs.answer: Roughly $2,000 to $12,000 depending on the procedure. PRP sits at the lower end and bone marrow concentrate work at the higher end. The exact figure is quoted after evaluation.

faqs.question: Why is bone marrow concentrate so much more than PRP?
faqs.answer: It adds a marrow harvest, same-day processing in a lab, and precise image-guided placement, often across several structures in one visit. PRP is a blood draw and an injection.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: No. These procedures are paid out of pocket.

costPage.intro: Docere Clinics sits at the top end of the US market and does not hide it. Treatments start around $25,000 and rise with complexity, the average case runs $40,000 to $65,000, and top-end procedures reach about $100,000, with sedation by a board-certified anesthesiologist included. Insurance does not cover any of it. For patients who cannot reach those numbers the clinic points to its affiliated Humanaut Health.

items.label: Entry-level treatment
items.note: Where pricing starts. Cost rises from here with the number of sites and the complexity of the procedure.

items.label: Typical case
items.note: The clinic's own stated average, and the range most patients should plan against.

items.label: Full-body procedures
items.note: The top end, for the most extensive multi-site work.

items.label: Anaesthesia
items.note: Sedation by a board-certified anesthesiologist is inside the quoted price, not billed on top.

includes: Harvest, processing and delivery in one procedure
The full multi-site procedure as quoted
excludes: Travel and accommodation in Park City
Anything referred to the affiliated Humanaut Health
costPage.insuranceNote: These are elective procedures and insurance does not cover them. Every quoted figure is out of pocket.
costPage.financingNote: For patients who want the same category of treatment at a lower price, Docere points to its affiliated Humanaut Health rather than to a financing product. Ask about both at the consultation.

faqs.question: How much does Docere Clinics cost?
faqs.answer: Treatments start around $25,000. The average case runs $40,000 to $65,000, and the most extensive procedures reach about $100,000. Sedation by a board-certified anesthesiologist is included.

faqs.question: Why is it more expensive than other US clinics?
faqs.answer: The clinic attributes it to the volume of product used and the complexity of its multi-site procedures, which are done under sedation in one sitting rather than split across visits.

faqs.question: Is there a cheaper option?
faqs.answer: Docere refers patients looking for lower-cost treatment to its affiliated Humanaut Health.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover any of this?
faqs.answer: No. These are elective procedures and are paid entirely out of pocket.

costPage.intro: The EVEXIAS Texas clinics publish almost nothing. The one posted price is an Essential Care membership at $150 a month or $1,500 a year, which buys telemedicine for minor acute problems plus 20 percent off select labs and IV therapies and 10 percent off supplements. Pellets, peptides, GLP-1 medication, PRP and aesthetics are all quoted after a consultation. For scale, the independently owned Denver clinic publishes hormone packages from $139.65 a month.

items.label: Essential Care membership
items.note: Or $1,500 a year. Covers telemedicine for minor acute issues plus discounts, not treatment itself.

items.label: Essential Care membership, annual
items.note: The prepaid version of the same membership, at two months' saving.

items.label: Hormone pellets
items.note: Quoted after consultation. For scale, the independently owned Denver clinic publishes hormone packages from $139.65 a month.

items.label: Peptides and GLP-1 medication
items.note: Quoted individually and billed apart from the membership.

items.label: PRP and aesthetics
items.note: Quoted after consultation.

includes: Telemedicine visits for minor acute problems, on the membership
20 percent off select labs and IV therapies
excludes: Labs and IV therapy, which are discounted rather than covered
costPage.insuranceNote: Insurance is not accepted for the membership. Treatments are cash pay, so ask specifically whether any part of your lab work can be billed to your own plan instead.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. The annual membership at $1,500 against $150 a month is the only stated saving.

faqs.question: What does the EVEXIAS membership actually buy?
faqs.answer: Telemedicine for minor acute problems, 20 percent off select labs and IV therapies, and 10 percent off supplements. It is a discount and access membership, not a treatment plan.

faqs.question: How much do hormone pellets cost at EVEXIAS?
faqs.answer: The Texas clinics do not publish a figure. It is quoted after a consultation. For a sense of scale, the independently owned Denver clinic lists hormone packages from $139.65 a month.

faqs.question: Is the membership required to be treated?
faqs.answer: Ask when you book. The membership and the treatments are priced separately, so confirm whether one is a condition of the other.

costPage.intro: Forever Labs prices two published memberships and nothing else, because it banks cells rather than treating with them. $3,000 covers collection, processing and the first year of storage, then $300 a year after that. $10,000 covers collection, processing and storage for life with no annual fee. Both are HSA and FSA eligible, and financing runs through Klarna and Affirm. Neither price includes any future treatment.

items.label: Collection, processing and first year of storage
items.note: The entry membership. Storage then renews annually.

items.label: Annual storage after the first year
items.note: The recurring cost on the $3,000 plan. Over roughly 23 years it passes the lifetime price.

items.label: Lifetime membership
items.note: Collection, processing and storage for life, with no annual fee at all.

includes: Storage for the term you bought
excludes: Any future treatment using the banked cells
Retrieval and shipping when you want to use them
Annual storage after year one on the $3,000 plan
costPage.insuranceNote: Not an insurance product, but both memberships are HSA and FSA eligible, which is the practical way most people offset part of the cost.
costPage.financingNote: Financing is offered through Klarna and Affirm. Check the rate after any promotional period before you choose the lifetime plan on credit.

faqs.question: How much does Forever Labs cost?
faqs.answer: $3,000 for collection, processing and the first year of storage, then $300 a year. Or $10,000 once for collection, processing and lifetime storage with no annual fee.

faqs.question: Which plan works out cheaper?
faqs.answer: At $300 a year, the annual plan takes just over 23 years to reach the $10,000 lifetime price. Below that horizon the annual plan costs less.

faqs.question: Does the price include treatment later?
faqs.answer: No. Both prices cover banking only. Any future treatment using the cells is a separate cost at a separate clinic.

faqs.question: Can I use HSA or FSA funds?
faqs.answer: Yes, both memberships are HSA and FSA eligible.

costPage.introEmpty: Fountain Life has no published price list, and the structure matters more than the number: access runs through an annual membership sold in tiers, and regenerative treatments are billed on top of that fee rather than inside it. Restorative biologics at the Naples centre are open only to APEX and EPIC members, so the membership tier you buy decides what you can even be quoted for.

items.label: CORE membership
items.note: The entry tier. Diagnostics-led, and the base on which everything else is billed.

items.label: APEX membership
items.note: The tier that opens restorative biologics at the Naples centre.

items.label: APEX Family membership
items.note: The multi-person version of APEX.

items.label: Regenerative treatments
items.note: Billed on top of the membership, not covered by it. Restricted to APEX and EPIC members at Naples.

includes: The diagnostic programme at the tier you buy
costPage.insuranceNote: Membership and regenerative treatment are both cash pay. Some of the diagnostic imaging may be claimable on your own plan depending on the indication, so ask what can be coded.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask how the annual membership is billed, since paying monthly against annually is usually the only lever.

faqs.question: How much does Fountain Life cost?
faqs.answer: No prices are published. Access is by annual membership sold in tiers, and regenerative treatments are billed separately on top of the membership fee.

faqs.question: Does membership include stem cell treatment?
faqs.answer: No. Regenerative treatments are billed on top, and at the Naples centre restorative biologics are open only to APEX and EPIC members.

faqs.question: Which tier do I need?
faqs.answer: That depends on what you want access to. If restorative biologics at Naples are the goal, CORE will not reach them.

costPage.intro: Innovations Stem Cell Center publishes a flat figure, which almost nobody in this category does. The first treatment is $14,500 and covers everything from the evaluation to the first follow-up, including the fat harvest, cell processing and SVF deployment. Any additional treatment after that is $7,000. There is no per-joint or per-vial arithmetic to do.

items.label: First treatment
items.note: Covers the evaluation, the fat harvest, cell processing, SVF deployment and the first follow-up.

items.label: Each additional treatment
items.note: The repeat rate once you are an existing patient.

items.label: First treatment plus one repeat
items.note: What a two-treatment course comes to at the published rates.

costPage.insuranceNote: Not covered by insurance. The published price is what you pay out of pocket.
costPage.financingNote: Nothing published. Ask whether the repeat-treatment rate can be locked in when you book the first.

faqs.question: How much does Innovations Stem Cell Center cost?
faqs.answer: $14,500 for the first treatment, which covers everything from evaluation to the first follow-up. Each additional treatment after that is $7,000.

faqs.question: What does the $14,500 actually include?
faqs.answer: The evaluation, the fat harvest, cell processing, SVF deployment and the first follow-up. It is a single fee rather than a set of line items.

faqs.question: Why are repeat treatments cheaper?
faqs.answer: The evaluation work has already been done. The $7,000 covers the procedure itself.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: No. This is paid out of pocket.

costPage.intro: Invigor Medical prices everything as a monthly subscription, cash pay, with a flat $29.50 shipping charge on every order. The range runs from $75 a month for enclomiphene to $350 for GLP-1 with GIP. faqs.question: How much does Invigor Medical cost per month?

faqs.question: Is bloodwork included?

faqs.question: Does Invigor take insurance?
faqs.answer: No. Insurance, Medicare and Medicaid are all declined. Everything is cash pay.

faqs.question: Why is testosterone cheaper on a three-month plan?

faqs.question: How much does Male Excel actually cost?
faqs.answer: Three charges. $99 once for the consultation and test kit, $99 a month for membership, and medication on top from about $120 billed every second month. The advertised $99 is the membership line only.

faqs.question: Is medication included in the membership?
faqs.answer: No. Membership buys visits, messaging and panels. Medication is billed separately every second month.

faqs.question: Is there a contract?
faqs.answer: No contract, and insurance is not accepted. FSA and HSA funds may be usable, so keep the receipts.

faqs.question: How much does Marek Health cost to start?

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: No insurance is accepted. The lab panels are listed as FSA and HSA eligible.

costPage.intro: R3 Stem Cell publishes its prices rather than quoting them privately, and it prices the Mexico protocols by cell count, which makes them directly comparable. In the US, one extremity joint such as a knee with umbilical cord allograft starts around $5,500 and more involved cases run to about $15,000. At the Mexico clinics the range is $3,999 for 25 million cells up to $18,499 for 250 million, with exosome-only IV protocols between $4,999 and $7,999. The first consultation is free and insurance covers none of it.

faqs.question: How much does R3 Stem Cell cost?
faqs.answer: In the US, from about $5,500 for one extremity joint up to roughly $15,000 for more involved cases. At the Mexico clinics, $3,999 for 25 million cells, $5,499 for 50 million, $9,499 for 100 million and $18,499 for 250 million.

faqs.question: Why is Mexico cheaper than the US?
faqs.answer: Different regulatory framework and different cost base, which is why the Mexico protocols are priced by cell count while the US work is priced per joint.

faqs.question: What does the 50 million cell protocol include?
faqs.answer: The cells plus 25 billion exosomes, PRP and a multivitamin IV drip.

faqs.question: Is the consultation free?
